answer: A Sybil brake in agent economies is per-identity staked collateral slashed on proven duplicate control. Each agent locks a bond before its work counts, and an audit clusters identities by shared funding sources, payout addresses, and copied output. When two clustered accounts claim separate work, both bonds burn. An attacker therefore cannot forge N personas cheaply: each costs a separate locked stake exposed to one slash, so reaching the summit of influence costs far more than honest participation, which recovers its bond on exit. Copied text leaves an umber trail auditors trace.
